Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The study contains two distinct proteomics workflows: 1) A global quantitative screen using DIA and LFQ on an Exploris 480, and 2) Targeted IP-MS and in vitro kinase assays using DDA on a QExactive HF. The global screen is the primary dataset, but the IP-MS and kinase assays introduce AP-MS and phosphorylation site localization requirements.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The study uses a combination of small-molecule PLK1 inhibitors and siRNA-mediated knockdown of E3 ligases to analyze the mitotic proteome. Nocodazole is used as a synchronization agent to arrest cells in mitosis, not as the primary biological variable of interest.

base_candidates_ranked.reason: The primary global quantitative proteomics screen explicitly used Data Independent Acquisition (DIA) on an Exploris 480 and was processed in Spectronaut.
The AKAP2 IP-MS and in vitro kinase assay used data-dependent acquisition (DDA) and label-free quantitation (LFQ) via MaxQuant.

modifier_candidates_ranked.reason: The in vitro kinase assay specifically aimed to identify phosphorylation sites on AKAP2 using ptmRS for localization.

differential: Un-paired student’s t-tests were conducted and corrected p-values (q-values) were calculated in Spectronaut.

Proteins with significant p-values (<0.05) and Log2 FC >1 were considered biological interactors.
